key_insight: Timing between force-signal peaks from an instrumented hammer distinguished cortical from trabecular bone and showed potential to warn against impacts causing lateral hinge fracture.
engineering_relevance: Impact-force monitoring could provide intraoperative feedback to help surgeons stop osteotome advancement before hinge rupture during open-wedge high tibial osteotomy.
method: Record hammer force–time signals during osteotome impacts until bone rupture.
Calculate τ, the time interval between the first and second impact peaks.
Use relative changes in τ to detect transitions between cortical and trabecular bone.
evidence_signal: Across 17 lower-limb specimens from nine cadaveric donors, τ was significantly lower in cortical bone; algorithm–surgeon differences in identifying trabecular entry were under two impacts in 71% of medial and 81% of lateral osteotomies.
watch_item: Clinical validation is needed: cadaveric transition-detection results do not establish reliable fracture prevention in patients.
paper_title: Using an instrumented hammer to predict the lateral hinge fracture in high tibial osteotomy: A cadaveric study
